overview.description: Gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the lining of the stomach and intestines, commonly referred to as stomach flu (though unrelated to influenza). It is typically caused by viral infections (rotavirus, norovirus), bacterial infections (E. coli, Salmonella), or parasites. The primary concern is dehydration due to fluid loss.
overview.prevalence: Extremely common; millions of cases worldwide annually, particularly affecting children.
overview.age_group: All ages; infants, elderly, and immunocompromised are at highest risk for severe dehydration.

types.name: Viral Gastroenteritis
types.description: Caused by norovirus (highly contagious in adults) or rotavirus (leading cause in infants). Self-limiting, resolving within 3-7 days.

types.name: Bacterial Gastroenteritis (Food Poisoning)
types.description: Caused by consuming food/water contaminated with Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, or E. coli. Can be severe, requiring antibiotics.
types.common_in: Areas with poor sanitation, consumption of undercooked food

severity_levels.name: Mild Gastroenteritis
severity_levels.frequency: Occasional loose stool, mild nausea, no fever
severity_levels.impact: Managed with oral rehydration and rest at home

severity_levels.name: Moderate Gastroenteritis
severity_levels.frequency: Multiple episodes of diarrhea/vomiting, low-grade fever, mild signs of dry mouth
severity_levels.impact: Requires active oral rehydration salts (ORS) monitoring and medical consult

severity_levels.name: Severe Gastroenteritis with Dehydration
severity_levels.frequency: Inability to keep liquids down, high fever, dark urine, extreme dizziness, lethargy
severity_levels.impact: Medical emergency. Requires hospitalization and intravenous (IV) fluid therapy

genetic_factors: No direct genetic cause; however, individuals lacking the FUT2 gene show natural resistance to norovirus infections
environmental_triggers: Eating contaminated or undercooked food (poultry, eggs, shellfish)
Contact with infected individuals or surfaces

primary_symptoms.name: Stomach Cramps & Pain
primary_symptoms.description: Abdominal cramping, bloating, and generalized tenderness in the stomach region.

primary_symptoms.name: Nausea and Vomiting
primary_symptoms.description: Frequent vomiting making it difficult to retain fluids.

warning_signs_of_attack: Signs of severe dehydration: dry mouth, lack of tears, little to no urination, extreme thirst
Bloody diarrhea (indicates invasive bacterial infection like Shigella)
Vomiting lasting more than 24 hours, preventing fluid retention
Confusion, dizziness, or fainting when standing up
symptoms_in_children: Sunken eyes, sunken fontanelle (soft spot) in infants
Irritability, extreme sleepiness, or difficulty waking up
No wet diapers for 6 hours or more
Dry mouth and tongue, crying with no tears

medical_history: History of travel, source of drinking water, exposure to sick contacts
Recent meals (specifically raw eggs, undercooked meat, or seafood)
Assessment of liquid intake and frequency of urination
physical_examination: Checking blood pressure and heart rate (tachycardia and hypotension indicate dehydration)
Checking skin turgor (elasticity of skin) and dry mucous membranes
Abdominal examination for bloating or local tenderness

diagnostic_tests.description: Measures sodium, potassium, and chloride levels in the blood.
diagnostic_tests.purpose: Evaluates severity of electrolyte imbalance from fluid loss

medicines.note: All medications should be taken only under the supervision of a licensed physician. Self-medication can be dangerous.

categories.purpose: Restore lost fluids and essential minerals/electrolytes to prevent dehydration

medicines.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)
medicines.form: Powder packet (dissolved in water), pre-mixed solution
medicines.dosage: Sip continuously after every loose stool
medicines.use_case: Essential first-line measure for all cases of gastroenteritis
side_effects: None when mixed in the correct water ratio

categories.purpose: Suppress nausea and vomiting, allowing the patient to retain oral fluids
Kill the specific bacteria causing gastroenteritis
categories.note: Not used for viral infections (ineffective) and avoided in certain E. coli strains to prevent hemolytic uremic syndrome

diet_and_nutrition.overview: Dietary choices support recovery and prevent further irritation of the inflamed intestines.

items.benefit: Low in fiber and easy to digest; bananas restore lost potassium
Provides hydration and sodium to replace lost electrolytes
Gentle on the stomach and provides slow-release energy
Temporary lactose intolerance often develops during gastroenteritis; makes diarrhea worse
items.frequency: Avoid until 48 hours after symptoms resolve

items.food: Greasy, Fatty, or Highly Seasoned Foods
items.benefit: Hard to digest and can trigger stomach spasms/cramps
High sugar concentrations draw water into the colon, worsening diarrhea (osmotic diarrhea)
